tasks.short: Record anesthesia and patient condition during procedures

steps.what: Identify anesthesia administrations and patient condition observations for the procedure record
Copy anesthesia type, amount and patient condition data into the procedure chart
Verify and record the exact anesthesia and patient condition chart entries

tasks.design: Test native anesthesia-record configuration in {OTHER} to reuse clinician-confirmed administrations and existing device observations. The anesthesiologist still captures administration facts, verifies the chart and records clinical interpretation; no medication delivery or patient monitoring is automated by this proposal.
tasks.previous_blocker: Verified administrations and readings may be copied into another chart section.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing device and record interfaces can reuse exact fields where locally supported and validated.
tasks.still_hard: Wrong-patient links, timing discrepancies, artefacts and facts not represented by a device.
tasks.human_edge: The clinician distinguishes a recorded signal from the patient's actual condition.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate chart copying while clinical observation and record responsibility remain.

reach.learn: Source versions, patient identity and event timing

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native anesthesia-record interfaces may reuse verified administration and monitor fields. No digest case establishes anesthesia charting time savings or suitable local device coverage.

assumptions: Boundary is recording during the procedure, excluding patient monitoring in task 7754, choosing anesthesia and administering it. One clinical observation is counted once in roll-ups; only record-specific capture and verification are included here.

OTHER means anesthesia information and clinical record system. In s1 the anesthesiologist verifies and captures patient/procedure ID, medication identity, actual amount and unit, route, administration time, administrator, observation time, measured value/unit and source version. All first-entry and record-specific confirmation time remains in 45%; no free structured medication event or patient-status flag is assumed.

Existing monitors produce readings only where already connected. The clinician verifies patient/device association and rejects artefacts in s1 and s3. Missing interfaces, incompatible units or uncertain administrations return to manual charting; device readings never establish clinical state automatically.

Test native record and device configuration first. Already automatic charting earns no additional labour saving. Eight extra focal hours count mapping changes, sample chart audits and unusual reconciliation; 6 other-role hours count clinical-system administrator interface and access maintenance.
unknowns: Existing record interfaces and duplicate-copy baseline
Local device association and chart validation requirements
research_questions: Does native field reuse remove actual copying after administration capture, chart checking and reconciliation are included?

already_counted.description: Record-specific observation verification and structured capture
Clinical chart checks and entry approval

incremental.description: Mapping checks, chart audits and extra reconciliation

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient/procedure chart entries, medication events, amounts, units, times, source observations and record versions checked in s3; changes void approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=45+30=75; gross 25%, net 17% after 8 focal upkeep. Range covers already automatic charts with no new saving through 16 points of duplicate copying removed minus 8 upkeep. First capture and clinical verification remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor anesthesia patients and respond to complications

steps.what: Monitor patient condition before, during and after anesthesia
Counteract adverse reactions or complications based on the clinical assessment

tasks.design: The anesthesiologist observes the patient and interprets existing anesthesia monitoring {OTHER}. Intervention and reassessment remain clinician work; alarms and existing device runtime do not create a new labour saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clinical assessment requires patient context and continuous interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing monitors support observation without replacing the clinician.
tasks.still_hard: Rapidly changing conditions and conflicting clinical signs.
tasks.human_edge: The clinician recognises uncertainty and takes responsibility for intervention.
tasks.altitude: Clinical monitoring and intervention responsibility stay unchanged.

reach.learn: Team communication and clinical authority boundaries

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: patient monitoring, intervention and reassessment remain human in this design; no autonomous anesthesia care capability is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is direct patient monitoring and response, excluding record copying in task 7756.

Existing monitors produce readings; the anesthesiologist produces the clinical assessment in s1 before intervention in s2. Patient response is observed after intervention during s2 before reassessment; no structured complication diagnosis is supplied free.
OTHER means anesthesia monitoring system. Use native monitoring displays first; existing runtime earns no human saving. Zero incremental upkeep because no new care automation is introduced.
unknowns: Local monitoring setup and team responsibilities
research_questions: Which aspects of assessment are absent from existing monitor signals?

approvals.approved_version: Exact clinician-selected intervention and current patient assessment checked in s2 before action; changed patient condition requires renewed judgement.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=65+35=100; net 0%. Monitoring and clinical response retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Decide recovery readiness for transfer or discharge

steps.what: Decide when patients have recovered or stabilized enough for transfer or discharge

tasks.design: The anesthesiologist assesses recovery and decides readiness using direct observation and the clinical record {OTHER}. A score or electronic status does not become an automatic discharge decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readiness depends on the patient's overall condition and the intended destination.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records support assessment without removing clinical judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising residual risk and gaps in recovery information.
tasks.human_edge: The clinician reconciles observations and takes responsibility for the decision.
tasks.altitude: Transfer and discharge authority remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: recovery-readiness assessment and transfer decisions remain clinician work; no automated readiness determination is established.

assumptions: Boundary is the anesthesiologist's readiness decision, excluding transport, bed allocation and separate nursing observations.
Recovery staff provide existing observations; the anesthesiologist examines applicability and current condition during s1. No free structured recovered-enough flag is assumed.
OTHER means clinical record system. Check native record access first; existing runtime earns no saving. Zero new upkeep because no new decision tool is introduced.
research_questions: Which readiness decisions require additional direct assessment despite complete recorded observations?

already_counted.description: Recovery assessment and transfer or discharge approval

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient, current recovery assessment, destination and clinician decision checked in s1; changed condition or destination voids approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0%. Clinical readiness assessment retains all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Coordinate administration of anesthetics with surgeons during operation

tasks.design: The anesthesiologist coordinates directly with the surgeon during the operation. Existing information in the clinical record {OTHER} can support preparation but does not replace live team communication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Timing depends on surgical progress and the patient's condition.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing information access supports the conversation without removing it.
tasks.still_hard: Maintaining shared understanding when the operative situation changes.
tasks.human_edge: The clinician hears intent, clarifies and adapts with the surgical team.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: live anesthetic coordination remains human; documentation savings do not establish saved operative conversation time.

assumptions: Boundary is coordination with surgeons, excluding administration execution, monitoring in task 7754 and chart copying in task 7756.
The surgical team produces progress information during s1 and the anesthesiologist assesses current patient context there; no free structured safe-administration signal is assumed.
OTHER means clinical record system. Use existing information access first; native runtime earns no saving. Zero incremental upkeep because no communication automation is introduced.
unknowns: Operative workflow and team communication practices
research_questions: Which communication failures require direct clarification during an operation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0%. All live coordination remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Clinical judgement and operative coordination stay with the anesthesiologist; native chart reuse offers conditional copying savings.
reach: Coordinate traceable observations and handoffs with the care team.
role.ambitious_version: More reliable anesthesia records with patient observation and decision time fully protected.
